turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not here to fear anyone, Sandip. My concerns are for the well-being of my people and the stability of my land. I have no patience for your provocations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your tenantry, you say? They are not cowed by a weakling like you, Nikhil. They know who truly stands for their betterment and progress. But fear not, I shall not provoke them needlessly.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not a weakling, Sandip. My people respect me for my principles and stability. Your actions may bring temporary gains, but they sow the seeds of unrest. I demand you cease your interference and leave my lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your principles, Nikhil? They are but empty echoes in the hollow chambers of your mind. My actions, on the other hand, are the beating heart of progress and change. And as for your lands, they are not merely soil and stone—they are the canvas upon which I paint my vision of a new India.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your vision, Sandip, is one of chaos and division. I see only the suffering it will bring. I warn you, cease your interference or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Chaos and division, you say? My dear Nikhil, you mistake the tempest for the calm. Your lands shall see a dawn that you cannot comprehend, a dawn painted in the colors of freedom and justice. Your warnings mean little to me, for I am the storm that will cleanse the old order.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance blinds you, Sandip. The people I care for are not pawns in your grand designs. Cease your schemes or face the reality of my resolve.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your resolve, Nikhil? It is but a shadow in the light of my conviction. The people you claim to care for shall see the dawn I bring, whether you stand in its way or not.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your conviction is nothing but a mask for your recklessness, Sandip. The people will suffer under your rule, and I will not let that happen. Cease your destructive path or I will take action.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your resolve is commendable, my dear Nikhil, but it is like a candle in the sun. The people you speak of will see through the veil of oppression you uphold. My path is lit by their hope and my conviction. I shall not falter.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words ring hollow, Sandip. The people's suffering is real, and your so-called dawn will only bring more darkness. I warn you again, cease your harmful actions or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your warnings fall on deaf ears, Nikhil. The people yearn for a leader who will bring them out of the shadows and into the light. They will see that your resolve is but a fragile shield against the tide of change.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance blinds you, Sandip. The people may yearn for change, but they will suffer under your rule. My resolve is not just a shield, it is a duty to protect them from the likes of you.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your resolve, dear Nikhil, is as brittle as the glass you hide behind. The people will soon see that your shield crumbles in the face of their longing for a brighter future. My path is their hope, and I shall not be swayed.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your path is one of deception and tyranny, Sandip. The people may be blind to it now, but they will see the truth in time. I will not let you harm my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your melodramatic bluster is as predictable as the sunrise. You fear change because it threatens your comfortable illusions of righteousness. The people will choose their own path, and it will be paved with the fiery passion of those who dare to dream.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am caught between two men who see the world so differently. Sandip speaks of passion and change, while Nikhil warns of tyranny and suffering. How can I choose?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words are hollow, Sandip. The people may be drawn to your charisma now, but they will turn against you when they see the true face of your rule. My duty is clear.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh Bimala, darling, do not let the shadows of fear obscure the light of truth. Nikhil's words are the whispers of the past, while I am the herald of a new dawn.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel torn, as if a storm is raging inside me. Sandip's words ignite a fire of hope, but Nikhil's warnings chill my heart with fear.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
